shortDescription: West African crude oil differentials rose on Friday as renewed conflict in the Middle East and subsequent disruptions to supply incentivised buyers to look elsewhere.

children: West African crude oil differentials rose on Friday as renewed conflict in the Middle East and subsequent disruptions to supply incentivised buyers to look elsewhere.
BB Energy bid for a cargo of Congolese Djeno with October 3-8 dates at a $5.10 discount to dated Brent in the Platts window on Friday, but no sellers stepped in to hit the bid.

Nigerian Bonga was offered at dated plus $9 in the over-the-counter market, according to one trader, firmer than the levels closer to dated plus $5 other market participants discussed earlier in the week.
Bonga is around a $1 premium to Forcados, the source said.
Values in the West African market picked up in recent days as buyers increasingly look for supplies outside of the Middle East amid an intensifying conflict between the U.S. and Iran.

Four commodity vessels transited the key waterway of the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, down from nine a day earlier and well below the 10-day average tally of about 15, preliminary shipping data showed.

Nigeria's Dangote Group plans to price the initial public offering of its refinery unit at 525 naira ($0.40) per share, potentially raising about $1.5 billion in Africa's biggest-ever share sale, two sources with direct knowledge of the deal told Reuters on Friday.
At least 37 people died after inhaling fumes as they tried to tap an oil pipeline in southern Nigeria, an environmental group said on Friday, though authorities have not confirmed the toll.
